note: Small wooded tract on Rock Creek Road near the Platte River, with primitive camping at a small gravel lot south of the road; both tracts flood. --Claude
summary: Confirmed: MDC-designated primitive camping (area page 'Individual Campsites'; map's Primitive Camping Area at the gravel lot), free, FCFS, 14-night limit, no hookups. Pin is the MDC camping point, 40 m from the lot. Not waterfront confirmed. Tiny lot and flood-prone - flagged.
flags: INCLUSION/FIT: the area page lists 'Individual Campsites' and the 2007 area map puts its one Primitive Camping Area symbol at the gravel parking lot on the south side of Rock Creek Road; MDC GIS has one camping point (39.62690,-94.73112), 40 m south of that lot (39.62725,-94.73123). On imagery the lot is a single small gravel pull-in (~11 x 22 m) off the gravel county road, with only a footpath beyond it into the woods - so in practice the rig camps on the lot itself. It is an MDC-designated camping area (not a parking-lot allowance by MDC's own map), and a 23-ft rig can turn in from a flat gravel road, but there is room for about one rig. The MDC GIS record for the lot says 'Allows_Trailers: No' (the same value appears on every lot in all four MDC areas in this batch, so it reads as a boat-trailer flag, not a camping rule). The area page warns 'Both tracts are prone to flooding.'
WATERFRONT (stored not waterfront): confirmed. The Platte River is ~180 m north of the lot across Rock Creek Road through woods; Rock Creek is a small drainage.
Pin 39.62690,-94.73112 is the MDC camping point, 40 m from the lot - fine (the lot itself, 39.62725,-94.73123, would also do).
Note rewritten: generic MDC text (14-day limit, 'site length not published', directions) dropped - fields or the policy row carry it.
